## 🚦 v1.1.0.2 — Live control, notifications & no more lockouts

**Recommended update for everyone.** Install it from **Dashboard → Plugins** (your server picks the right build), then restart Jellyfin.

| Jellyfin server | Version | File |
|---|---|---|
| 10.11.0 → 10.11.x | `1.1.0.2` | `StreamLimit-v1.1.0.2.zip` |
| 12.0 → 12.x | `1.1.1.2` | `StreamLimit-v1.1.0.2-jellyfin12.zip` |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Administrators are now exempt from stream limits by default.** Turn off *Exempt administrators* in the plugin settings to limit them again.

### ✨ New
- **Live view of active streams** — the settings page lists every counted stream (user, device, client, title, IP, direct play or transcode), refreshed every 5 seconds. **Stop** and **Stop + log out** take effect immediately: the download is cut and the slot is freed, so the blocked device can start right away.
- **Webhook notifications** (#7) — get notified when a stream is blocked, and optionally when an admin stops one. Discord webhooks get a formatted embed; any other URL receives JSON that works with **Apprise** (Telegram, ntfy, e-mail…) and generic webhooks. A **Send test** button checks your setup.
- **Smarter blocked message** — use `{{user}}`, `{{active}}`, `{{limit}}` and `{{devices}}` in the title and text, e.g. *"Already playing on: Living-room TV"*. Works in the web popup and in the server message.
- **Activity log** (#7) — every block is recorded in **Dashboard → Activity** with user, device, client and IP (at most one entry per device every 5 minutes).
- **Sidebar entry** — *Stream Limiter* now has its own entry in the dashboard menu.

### 🐛 Fixes
- **No more lockouts after a stop.** Some clients keep their session alive after being stopped (AFinity, Swiftfin after a playback error, the Android app's native player). Those devices no longer count against the limit.
- **Clients that can't receive commands are now stopped on the server side**, so their stream stops counting too.
- **Legacy tokens are recognised.** On Jellyfin 12, clients sending `X-Emby-Token` (or the `Emby` auth scheme) to stream URLs could slip past the hard block.
- **The web popup is always on top**, above the buffering spinner of newer jellyfin-web versions, and blocks on `fetch()` requests are detected too.
- A deleted user's limit is now removed from the configuration.

### 🔧 Under the hood
- **The web message no longer edits `index.html` on disk** — it is added as the page is served. It works with read-only web folders (Docker), needs no restart when toggled, never runs a stale cached script after an update (Android webviews included), and the tag left by older versions is cleaned up automatically (also on uninstall).
- Verified end to end on **Jellyfin 10.11.11** and **Jellyfin 12.3**.
- Stricter build checks so every release loads on all 10.11.x and 12.x servers, and CI on every push and pull request.

### 📦 Install
Add the repository in **Dashboard → Plugins → Repositories**, then install **StreamLimiter** from the catalog:
```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JellyboxAD/Jellyfin.Plugin.StreamLimit/main/manifest.json
```

> [!TIP]
> If the plugin shows *NotSupported* after updating: uninstall it, restart, reinstall it from the catalog and restart again. Your limits and settings are kept.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/JellyboxAD/Jellyfin.Plugin.StreamLimit/compare/v1.1.0.1...v1.1.0.2
